title: OpenAI's rumored ChatGPT phone is coming from Apple's favorite supplier
excerpt: A ChatGPT smartphone may be coming in 2027, and may be built by Foxconn.
content_html:
Published Nov 19, 2026, 9:32 AM EST

Mark has been covering smart devices for the better part of a decade now, having started with Digital Trends in 2017. In that time, he's written about everything from budget phones to flagship phones, e-readers, smartwatches, fitness trackers, and anything else that might connect to a smartphone in some way. 

With a background in accessories, he's unusually obsessed with stuff that clips onto or connects to phones, and he loves when a new accessory comes across his desk.

He worked for Digital Trends from 2017 to 2025.

OpenAI is reportedly working alongside the Apple supplier Foxconn to create a ChatGPT-powered smartphone, separate from the Apple and Google duopoly.

The as-yet-unnamed OpenAI smartphone aims to release in 2027, and will allegedly include a 2nm processor, and, surprising nobody, a ton of hardware that should make it an AI powerhouse.

OpenAI working with Apple's favorite supplier

Foxconn has the experience to help OpenAI make a real smartphone

We've seen a lot of companies try to overturn iOS's and Android's stranglehold on the smartphone market, but to date, none have really succeeded.

But the AI boom clearly has people thinking a new hegemony has room to rise, and with Amazon taking a second stab at a smartphone, it makes sense others would also be willing to try.

We've known OpenAI is looking to create its own smartphone for the better part of this year, but now, it seems plans are starting to come to fruition, with phone manufacturing veteran Foxconn tapped to bring it to life.

According to a report from Securities Times (via Abhishek Yadav on X), Foxconn's subsidiary, FIH Mobile, has managed to snag the order to create smartphones for OpenAI. It has also been claimed by another source that OpenAI would be looking to have units on sale by the back end of 2027. This matches with earlier reports that OpenAI would want production to have begun by early 2027.

We don't know a huge amount about the phone itself. According to noted analyst Ming-Chi Kuo, the phone will have a 2nm MediaTek Dimensity 9600 processor, two dedicated AI processing units, LPDDR6 RAM, and UFS 5.0 storage. So really, what you'd imagine from a phone that's likely to put AI first and foremost.

Quite how the phone's software will function is another question entirely. An Android fork would be the most obvious and easiest way for OpenAI to proceed, but there's always the chance it decides to create an entirely new operating system itself.

Though, with a potential launch at the end of next year, that may be a little ambitious. That said, AI companies are nothing but optimistic and ambitious, so I wouldn't rule this out at all.

Another question is whether consumers even want this. Right now, you can get access to ChatGPT on Android and iPhone through OpenAI's apps. Are people likely to move over to a completely new and untested ecosystem just because of the lure of ChatGPT? It's a long bet, but personally, given how history has shown us consumers are averse to change, I would say not.

But, with the AI market being as it is, good sense left the conversation a long time ago. OpenAI has previously spoken about selling more smartphones than Samsung, just in case you were wondering how high its eyes were set. It's clear it will throw as much money as possible at this project. That is, if it's able to — it does have an ongoing legal battle with Apple that may slow it down.
